correctness.rationale: Phi′/Phi=1+sec(-ω)+tan(-ω). Positive Taylor coefficients for U(w)=sec w+tan w follow from U′=(1+U²)/2 and yield the exact pointwise phase bound at ω=-s. Writing ω=z^mη and Schwarz–Pick for η gives (1-r²)|ω′|<=m(1-r²)s/r+r^m-s²/r^m. For each s<=r^m a real disk automorphism η=(c-z)/(1-cz) has ω(r)=-s and derivative aligned, so the radial optimization is attained. Direct Schwarz–Pick for ω then yields G(s)=(1-s²)(1+sec s+tan s); the logarithmic derivative of the monotonic critical-ratio R(s) is positive on (0,1), proving unique maximizing r*. Independently evaluated the transcendental equation with 50-digit arithmetic at r*=0.27327758869480084986 and G(r*)=2.14565700788682289571. For m>=2, a Blaschke family with sample radius R tending to 1 approaches G(r*), while interior equality in Schwarz–Pick would make ω an automorphism, impossible with ω′(0)=0. At r=0 the envelopes are 2 for m=1 and 0 for m>=2.

value.rationale: Exact pre-Schwarzian norm and hyperbolic radial envelope are natural distortion invariants for a specific analytic derivative class. The fact that every finite Taylor jet retains the same global supremum but m>=2 loses interior extremizers describes a meaningful sharp boundary phenomenon.
residual_risks: The global upper estimate is a standard composition of Schwarz–Pick and a radial target maximum; object-specific sharpness and finite-jet extremal phenomenon carry the value, not a claim of new general distortion theory.

final_claim: For derivative subordination f′(z)=e^{ω(z)}(1+sin ω(z)), ω=O(z^m), the exact radial pre-Schwarzian envelope is a one-variable maximization; all m share sharp global norm 2.14565700788682... with no interior equality when m>=2.
